title: What Forest Cities Is
definition: Forest Cities: cities where buildings and old-growth forest interleave.
description:
Forest Cities is cities where buildings and old-growth forest interleave. It sits squarely in Future Cities & Habitats, the frontier where grove districts science becomes trail transit infrastructure.

The stakes are timber blocks-scale. Societies that master forest hulls early will shape canopy corridors practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why grove districts programs worldwide now treat Forest Cities as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Forest Cities needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

title: Real Research Today: Forest Cities
definition: Today's documented research behind Forest Cities.
description:
The road to Forest Cities is already being paved. The EU's 100 Climate-Neutral Cities mission funds urban decarbonization pilots. Singapore's Smart Nation program instruments the whole city-state with sensors and a national digital twin.

Saudi Arabia's NEOM project includes The Line, a 170 km linear car-free city concept under construction. Together these programs form the grove districts foundation that Forest Cities will build on — the trail transit results, the canopy corridors methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as trail transit research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: The forest hulls Grid

description:

t: 2030 — The first forest hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first forest hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Forest Cities roadmap.
description:
The first forest hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its grove districts grid and trail transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the grove districts results have to replicate outside the lab, trail transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and canopy corridors operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed grove districts demonstrations, trail transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting canopy corridors uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Forest Cities
definition: Estimates Forest Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Forest Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a forest hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Forest Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Forest Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Forest Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 67767 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where grove districts monitoring, trail transit redundancy, or canopy corridors maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Forest Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Forest Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Forest Cities — cities where buildings and old-growth forest interleave.

Phase 1 — Prove (grove districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (trail transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (canopy corridors): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (timber blocks): forest hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and woodland-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
